correctness.rationale: For D,R,q>0 and a fully absorbing disk, the backward Dirichlet inverse at v=0 maps first-derivative forcing to a higher Sobolev regularity class, so the drift is a bounded perturbation after inversion and the small-v expansion is justified. The passive time gives first-order forcing rho/(2D). Substituting F=(R I_1(k rho)/I_1(kR)-rho)/(2Dq) into the second harmonic gives forcing -(F'-F/rho)/2=-Rk I_2(k rho)/(4Dq I_1(kR)); the angular Laplacian contributes -4q. Applying the radial operator to I_2(k rho) and I_2(2k rho) yields the particular solution and the regular homogeneous correction, respectively. With L=kR, z=k rho, c=I_2(L)/I_2(2L), positivity follows from strict increase of I_2(2z)/I_2(z); strictness of the derivative follows from the positive-coefficient ratio covariance with j and 4^j. The same argument on I_2'(z)/z gives strict decrease of I_2'(z)/(2I_2'(2z)) from 1/4 to below c at z=L; thus exactly one strict interior maximum. Taylor expansion gives k^4 rho²(R²-rho²)/32 for the leading Bessel bracket, with uniform remainder over the closed disk, and hence the stated H-limit and peak at R/sqrt(2). For large L, at z=L-s the derivative ratio divided by c tends to e^s/2 uniformly on bounded s; testing fixed s below and above log 2 brackets the unique root. The normalized profile e^(-s)-e^(-2s) then gives peak height R/(48D^(3/2)q^(3/2)). Independent Bessel series and bisection at R=D=1 support both regimes, including wall distances 0.7101802, 0.7040833 and 0.6990514 at L=10,20,40.

value.rationale: The second harmonic resolves directional variation that disappears in the known orientation average. The theorem identifies the unique radius of strongest quadratic directional response at every rotational diffusivity and distinguishes a true interior optimum at slow rotation from a shrinking wall layer at fast rotation, with explicit location and height constants. These are concrete checks for numerical first-passage calculations and are not obtainable from the zero-harmonic result.
residual_risks: A coefficient maximum is not a radial optimum of the full finite-speed mean first-exit time.
